q:
בת 94, גרה לבדה עד האשפוז, לא ידוע על ירידה קוגניטיבית. מאושפזת במחלקה פנימית בשל אלח דם (SEPSIS) ממקור של דלקת בדרכי השתן. היא נושאת קתטר שתן ומטופלת באנטיביוטיקה דרך הוריד. רופא גריאטר נקרא לתת יעוץ בשל מצב של אי-שקט ובלבול. בבדיקה נראית כאובה, סובלת מאי שקט פסיכו-מוטורי בולט, ליקוי בקשב, חוסר התמצאות במקום ובזמן. רשימת תרופות שמקבלת:   
 ROCEPHIN  
 ENOXAPARIN (CLEXAN)  
 PARACETAMOL  
 OXAZEPAM (VABEN)  
 RAMIPRIL (TRITACE)  
 TROSPIUM (SPASMEX)  
 BROTIZOLAM (BONDORMIN)  
 מה צריך לייעץ בהתייחס לטיפול התרופתי שהמטופלת מקבלת?
o: להפסיק טיפול ב- VABEN שקיבלה בביתה
להפסיק את הטיפול ב- TROSPIUM (SPSMEX)
להחליף את ה-BROTIZOLAM (BONDORMIN) ב- ZOLPIDEM (ZODORM)
להוסיף טיפול קבוע ב- TRAMADOL לאיזון כאב
explanation:
IMA key (2020 Q51) — **Stop trospium**.

Beers lists “Trospium” under strong bladder antimuscarinics. In a patient with sepsis, inattention and fluctuating agitation, reviewing that anticholinergic exposure addresses a possible contributor to delirium. Other precipitating factors still need treatment.

**A. Stop the oxazepam taken at home.** Prolonged use can produce physical dependence. Abrupt cessation may precipitate withdrawal and worsen delirium, so review the use history and plan any reduction.
**B. Stop trospium.** Trospium is listed among drugs with strong anticholinergic properties, a group that may worsen delirium.
**C. Replace brotizolam with zolpidem.** Switching does not remove the delirium risk: Z-drugs are also associated with delirium.
**D. Add regular tramadol for pain.** Adding an opioid requires pain assessment and consideration of delirium risk, rather than automatic scheduled treatment.

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2060, 2066, 2074; Hazzard 8e, pp. 888–889, 1061.

q: מטופל בן 72 עם דמנציה קלה-בינונית מגיע לחדר מיון עם חשד לאוטם שריר הלב. הוא מסרב לטיפול ואומר 'אני רוצה לחזור הביתה'. איך יש לנהוג?
o: לכבד את סירובו ולשחרר אותו מיד
להתחיל טיפול בכוח כי מדובר במצב מסכן חיים
לבחון את יכולתו לקבל החלטות מדעת ולפעול בהתאם
לבקש מבן המשפחה להחליט במקומו
explanation:
**הסכמה מדעת** דורשת הבנה ובחירה מרצון ביחס לטיפול המוצע. לכן, כהסקה מדרישות החוק, יש לברר מה המטופל מבין ומה משמעות סירובו לפני החלטה על שחרור או טיפול בניגוד לרצונו. החוק מסדיר בנפרד מצבי סכנה וחירום; חשד לאוטם אינו מבטל מעצמו את הצורך לבדוק את תנאיהם (סעיפים 13 ו־15, עמ׳ PDF 8 ו־15).
"לא יינתן טיפול רפואי למטופל אלא אם כן נתן לכך המטופל הסכמה מדעת לפי הוראות פרק זה." (עמ׳ 8).

**א. לכבד את סירובו ולשחרר אותו מיד.** שגויה, שחרור מיידי מדלג על הבירור אם הסירוב מבוסס על הבנת המצב והטיפול. זו הסקה מחובת מסירת מידע המאפשר החלטה מרצון (סעיף 13, עמ׳ PDF 8).
**ב. להתחיל טיפול בכוח כי מדובר במצב מסכן חיים.** שגויה, החוק אינו מתיר כפייה אוטומטית בכל סכנה: התנגדות בסכנה חמורה כפופה למסלול ועדת אתיקה ולתנאים, ובחירום נבחנת האפשרות לקבל הסכמה מדעת (סעיף 15, עמ׳ PDF 15).
**ג. לבחון את יכולתו לקבל החלטות מדעת ולפעול בהתאם.** נכונה, בדיקת ההבנה והבחירה מאפשרת להחליט אם מדובר בסירוב מדעת או במצב המחייב מסלול אחר לפי החוק; זו הסקה מדרישות סעיפים 13 ו־15 (עמ׳ PDF 8 ו־15).
**ד. לבקש מבן המשפחה להחליט במקומו.** שגויה, עצם הקרבה המשפחתית אינה המינוי המתואר בחוק. יש לברר סמכות ייצוג כדין במקום להחליף את החלטת המטופל אוטומטית בהחלטת קרוב (סעיף 16, עמ׳ PDF 16).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה; עמודי PDF, עמ׳ 8, 15, 16.
ref: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996 · PDF pp. 8–9, 15–16; sections 13, 14(a), 15
label: Source: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ״ו-1996 · PDF pp. 8–9, 15–16; sections 13, 14(a), 15

q: A patient has a stage 4 pressure injury over the sacrum. Which description matches this stage?
o: Full-thickness loss with exposed deep structures and osteomyelitis risk
Intact skin with nonblanchable erythema and preserved deeper tissue
Partial-thickness loss with a moist wound bed and a serum-filled blister
Visible subcutaneous fat with granulation and covered bone and tendon
explanation:
Pressure injury stage reflects anatomical tissue loss. **Stage 4 is full-thickness skin and tissue loss with exposed or directly palpable deep structures**, such as muscle, tendon or bone. Bone involvement raises concern for osteomyelitis.

**A. Deep structures exposed.** This distinguishes stage 4 from a full-thickness injury limited to subcutaneous tissue.
**B. Intact skin with nonblanching redness.** This is typical stage 1 pressure injury.
**C. Exposed moist dermis or serum blister.** These are stage 2 findings involving partial-thickness loss.
**D. Visible fat without exposed deep structures.** This fits stage 3.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 686–687.

q: In the study of patients with Parkinson disease or dementia described in Hazzard, honey-thick liquids were compared with nectar-thick liquids and chin-down posture. Which result distinguishes short-term aspiration from pneumonia during follow-up?
o: Less short-term aspiration and a lower follow-up pneumonia rate
More short-term aspiration and a lower follow-up pneumonia rate
Less short-term aspiration and a similar follow-up pneumonia rate
More short-term aspiration and a similar follow-up pneumonia rate
explanation:
In patients with Parkinson disease or dementia, honey-thick liquid most often prevented aspiration during fluoroscopy. Even with that consistency, about half the participants still aspirated, and follow-up showed no clear advantage for preventing pneumonia.

**A. Less aspiration and fewer pneumonias.** The immediate benefit was measurable, but the observed three-month pneumonia rate was numerically higher with honey-thick than with nectar-thick liquids.
**B. More aspiration and fewer pneumonias.** During testing, 53 percent aspirated with honey-thick liquid, compared with 63 percent with nectar-thick liquid and 68 percent with chin-down posture.
**C. Less aspiration and similar pneumonia rates.** Neither the pooled comparison with chin-down posture nor the comparison of the two viscosities showed a clear pneumonia advantage. Clinically important differences remained possible.
**D. More aspiration and similar pneumonia rates.** Similar follow-up rates are compatible with differences during testing, when honey-thick liquid produced the least aspiration.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 450. Logemann et al., JSLHR 2008, pp. 173–183 and Robbins et al., Ann Intern Med 2008, pp. 509–518.

q: A 77-year-old woman lives independently, manages her medications, and drives. Despite trazodone 50 mg nightly for three months, she reports fragmented sleep. MMSE is 28/30. Her diary records going to bed at 8 pm, falling asleep at 11 pm, repeated awakenings, and final waking at 4 am. She spends most days indoors watching television. Which behavioral approach is consistent with the source's sleep recommendations?
o: Advance bedtime further and remain in bed through prolonged wakefulness
Schedule prolonged daytime naps and vary the morning rising time
Increase moderate daytime activity and follow a consistent waking schedule
Schedule strenuous exercise just before bedtime and watch television in bed
explanation:
Long periods awake in bed can reinforce an association between bed and wakefulness, while sedentary days weaken sleep pressure. **Increase moderate daytime activity and use a consistent wake time**.

**A. Earlier bedtime and stay awake in bed.** Going to bed when sleepy and leaving bed during prolonged wakefulness better supports stimulus control.
**B. Long naps and variable rising.** These reduce sleep pressure and destabilize the sleep schedule.
**C. Daytime activity and regular waking.** Both help consolidate sleep and suit her current sedentary routine.
**D. Strenuous exercise just before bed and television in bed.** Late vigorous exercise and stimulating in-bed activity can interfere with sleep.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 661–662.

q: An 82-year-old man with vascular dementia is hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure. He is usually oriented to person but now fails to recognize his daughter, has difficulty sustaining attention, and was awake overnight trying to catch a bus. Which interpretation best fits the acute mental-status change?
o: Progression of dementia accounting for the overnight fluctuation
Delirium superimposed on dementia during acute illness
Stable baseline dementia accounting for the new inattention
Expected normal aging accounting for the abrupt confusion
explanation:
Dementia makes delirium more likely during acute illness. Overnight loss of recognition and inability to sustain attention are new compared with his baseline. **Delirium superimposed on dementia** best explains the timing during heart-failure decompensation.

**A. Dementia progression overnight.** Chronic progression alone rarely produces this abrupt change.
**B. Superimposed delirium.** The family describes a new disturbance of attention during a physiological stressor.
**C. Stable dementia.** The vignette specifically describes a departure from his usual behavior and recognition.
**D. Normal aging.** Abrupt confusion and inattention are pathological, not routine age-related change.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 881, 883.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp. 881, 883–885

q: A 77-year-old man with early Parkinson disease lives alone and independently manages his IADLs. His daughter requests power of attorney because she believes he has dementia. He has mild rest tremor, cogwheeling, and bradykinesia. MoCA is 24/30 with visuospatial and executive errors, but he accurately describes his medicines, manages finances online, and drives safely. Which response addresses the discrepancy between cognitive screening and function?
o: Arrange formal neuropsychological assessment of the cognitive findings
Treat the MoCA result as establishing loss of decision-making capacity
Diagnose Parkinson disease dementia from the screening result
Treat his independent function as excluding cognitive impairment
explanation:
Cognitive screening can detect subtle impairment in Parkinson disease even when daily independence is preserved. **Arrange formal neuropsychological assessment** to clarify his visuospatial and executive errors before making consequential judgments.

**A. Formal assessment.** A detailed cognitive profile can be interpreted alongside his independent finances and medication management.
**B. Declare loss of capacity.** Capacity is decision-specific and cannot be determined from a MoCA total alone.
**C. Diagnose Parkinson dementia.** Dementia requires cognitive impairment that interferes with everyday independence.
**D. Exclude impairment.** Mild cognitive impairment can coexist with preserved instrumental activities.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 153, 869, 870, 906.
ref: Hazzard Ch 57 — COGNITIVE CHANGES IN NORMAL AND PATHOLOGIC AGING
chapterTitle: Cognitive Changes in Normal and Pathologic Aging

q: A 74-year-old woman with depression and osteoarthritis has persistent hip pain despite acetaminophen. She takes sertraline and declines NSAIDs because of gastrointestinal concerns. The team is considering a supervised change to duloxetine. Which source-described action explains its potential analgesic role?
o: Inhibition of cyclooxygenase to reduce prostaglandin formation
Modulation of pain pathways through serotonin and norepinephrine
Blockade of voltage-gated calcium channels to reduce excitability
Increased GABA activity to reduce neuronal excitability
explanation:
Duloxetine is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor used as a coanalgesic. **It modulates pain signaling through serotonin and norepinephrine**, including descending inhibitory pathways.

**A. Cyclooxygenase inhibition.** This is an NSAID mechanism.
**B. Monoamine modulation.** Increasing serotonin and norepinephrine can strengthen descending pain inhibition.
**C. Calcium-channel action.** Gabapentinoids act at a calcium-channel subunit.
**D. Greater GABA activity.** This does not describe duloxetine's principal mechanism.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1063, 1064.

q: A patient with HFpEF receives diuretics for congestion. Excessive diuresis is followed by fatigue, lower blood pressure, and prerenal azotemia. Which hemodynamic change explains this volume sensitivity?
o: Increased ventricular filling volume with increased stroke volume
Increased ventricular filling volume with decreased stroke volume
Decreased ventricular filling volume with decreased stroke volume
Decreased ventricular filling volume with increased stroke volume
explanation:
A stiff HFpEF ventricle needs adequate filling to maintain forward output. **Overdiuresis decreases diastolic filling volume and stroke volume**, causing fatigue, relative hypotension and reduced kidney perfusion.

**A. More filling and more stroke volume.** Volume removal reduces filling in this scenario.
**B. More filling but less stroke volume.** Overdiuresis does not increase end-diastolic volume.
**C. Less filling and less stroke volume.** This explains the patient's signs of low forward output.
**D. Less filling but more stroke volume.** A stiff ventricle cannot compensate sufficiently when preload falls too far.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1186.

q: בן 73, סובל בחודשים האחרונים מכאב נוירופתי המפריע לו בחיי היום יום. מתוך התרופות האפשרויות לטיפול איזה מעקב נדרש בעקבות תופעת לוואי מתאימה?
o: ELATROLET (Amitriptyline) מעקב קצב לב כי גורם לברדיקרדיה
TEGRETOL (Carbamazepine) מעקב אלקטרוליטים כי גורם להיפוקלמיה
CYMBALTA (Duloxetine) מעקב לחץ דם כי מעלה לחץ דם
LYRICA (Pregabalin) מעקב תפקודי כבד כי גורם לפגיעה כבדית
explanation:
Adjuvant analgesics have class-specific adverse effects that guide monitoring. **Check blood pressure with duloxetine**, an SNRI whose noradrenergic action can raise it.

**A. Amitriptyline and bradycardia.** Anticholinergic tachycardia, orthostasis and conduction effects are more characteristic concerns.
**B. Carbamazepine and hypokalemia.** Hyponatremia is the characteristic electrolyte issue.
**C. Duloxetine and blood pressure.** Monitor at baseline and during treatment, especially with hypertension.
**D. Pregabalin and hepatic injury.** Review kidney function for dosing and monitor sedation and dizziness.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1063, 1064, 1065, 1647.

q: In the epidural steroid injection RCT of 400 older adults with lumbar spinal stenosis, what did adding glucocorticoid to lidocaine achieve?
o: Proof that lidocaine alone has no effect compared with placebo
Minimal or no additional short-term disability or leg-pain benefit
Proof that steroid injections outperform a placebo injection
A clear additional short-term disability and leg-pain benefit
explanation:
The 400-patient trial found minimal or no additional short-term disability or leg-pain benefit from adding glucocorticoid to lidocaine; it had no placebo arm (p1639).

D. A clear additional short-term disability and leg-pain benefit: The reported comparison showed minimal or no short-term benefit (p1639).
C. Proof that steroid injections outperform a placebo injection: The trial included no placebo group (p1639).
A. Proof that lidocaine alone has no effect compared with placebo: Without a placebo arm, that comparison was not made (p1639).

q: מה מהבאים מוגדר כאי ספיקת כליות חדה AKI באישה בת 70 ששוקלת 70 ק"ג?
o: עליה בקראטינין מ- 0.4 ל- 0.8 תוך 24 שעות
קראטינין 0.9 עם אלבומינוריה של 300 mg/g
מתן 400cc שתן ב 6 שעות
עליה באוריאה מ- 50 ל- 80 תוך 3 ימים
keySource: IMA 2026-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q124
explanation:
Acute kidney injury is defined by an acute creatinine rise from baseline or sufficiently low urine output. **A rise from 0.4 to 0.8 mg/dL in 24 hours meets AKI criteria**, even though the final value can fall within a laboratory reference interval.

**A. Creatinine doubles in 24 hours.** The absolute increase is 0.4 mg/dL and the value doubles, satisfying the relative as well as absolute criterion.
**B. Creatinine 0.9 with albuminuria.** Albuminuria indicates kidney damage but gives no evidence here of an acute fall in filtration.
**C. 400 mL urine in six hours at 70 kg.** This is about 0.95 mL/kg/hour, above the oliguria cutoff of 0.5.
**D. Urea rises over three days.** Urea varies with volume and catabolism. Its rise alone is not a diagnostic AKI criterion.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2372.

q: מה מהבאים מהווה את הסיבוך המאוחר ביותר של אוטם שריר הלב?
o: Left Ventricular Aneurysm
Ventricular Tachycardia
Papillary Muscle Rupture
Pericarditis
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 286 – ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q114
explanation:
A true LV aneurysm develops as an infarcted wall scars and remodels. **Left ventricular aneurysm is characteristically a late complication**, often becoming clinically important weeks to months after STEMI.

**A. LV aneurysm.** A scarred, dyskinetic segment can lead to heart failure, thrombus or ventricular arrhythmia.
**B. Ventricular tachycardia.** It can develop during acute ischemia, although scar-related VT can also occur later.
**C. Papillary muscle rupture.** This mechanical complication usually presents within days, often with abrupt severe mitral regurgitation.
**D. Pericarditis.** Early infarct-associated pericarditis can occur within days. Delayed immune-mediated pericarditis is a distinct possibility.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2122–2125.
